title: The Remnant
notes: This chunk is one of the book's strongest evidence assemblies: independent ratios from Solomon, Jeremiah, Elijah/Paul, Zechariah, Isaiah, field geometry, and gold ore converge on a narrow remnant band without padding. The tables and edition-conditioned blocks are clear and useful. Residual director staging remains in 'Weigh the chapter' and 'mark where,' and several author sentences open with And/But/That against house style. Print and web field sections also disagree on row spacing (handbreadth vs two handbreadths), which should track the table math. Fixes below are surgical openers and one factual alignment; doctrine and quoted scripture are left untouched.

This chunk stacks creation ratios, Job's household, extrabiblical counts, and land-capacity arithmetic into a tight case for the remnant near 0.2 percent, with clean tables and a strong convergence close. Strengths are the concrete chaining of independent lines and the law-positive density of the argument. Residual defects include three author sentences opening with And or That, director staging (hold that, Hold the, Now seat), an internal Job survivor mismatch (six with wife versus five in later tables and print summary), a household table that splits one Sabean raid into two rows, and a stray endif::[] markup tag. The fixes restore house style, count consistency, and clean AsciiDoc without altering doctrine or quoted text.

The chunk’s core strength is the four-word Hebrew remnant etymology, tightly linked to needle’s-eye and exceeding-righteousness images, plus a clean Ruth enactment of the gleaning household. Design-not-failure and the closing urgency paragraphs stay assertive and on-voice. Residual presenter staging remains in two “Now” constructions and a “weigh” cue; the print-only block opens with a forbidden And. No quote, doctrine, or factual defects appear. Minor colloquial “worth the dig” is the only other register slip.

proposals.new: __“the sym:sym-field[field] is the world”__ (Matthew 13:38) sets the scale: the larger the harvest, the smaller its edge — and the gleanings at that edge are, by the law's own terms, the sym:sym-poor[poor], the sym:sym-stranger[stranger], the sym:sym-fatherless[fatherless], and the sym:sym-widow[widow] of the Orphans and Widows chapter.

proposals.old: The edge of a field is fixed by mathematics: grain is sown in rows a handbreadth apart, and the perimeter row's share of the crop *shrinks as the field grows*.
proposals.new: The edge of a field is fixed by mathematics: grain is sown in rows roughly two handbreadths apart, and the perimeter row's share of the crop *shrinks as the field grows*.
proposals.summary: Align print row spacing with the web table math.
proposals.rationale: The web block and table use roughly two handbreadths; print's 'a handbreadth' contradicts that spacing and would change the edge percentages.

proposals.summary: Align early survivor count with later evidence table and print summary.
proposals.rationale: Later text and the convergence table consistently use five (four messengers plus Job); the early six-with-wife creates an internal mismatch.

proposals.old: Now hear the Lord again: __“It is easier for a camel to go through the *eye of a needle*, than for a sym:sym-rich[rich] man to enter into the kingdom”__ (Matthew 19:24) — and remember what the sym:sym-rich[rich] are in this book's vocabulary: the proud, the unbowed.

proposals.old: Now return to the question Jesus was asked, and weigh His answer with the numbers on the table.
proposals.new: The question Jesus was asked stands with the numbers on the table.
proposals.rationale: Both “Now return” and “weigh” are listed presenter staging; the claim is stronger when asserted without instructing the reader.

proposals.old: And the Hebrew keeps the picture in the remnant's own name: one of the words our Bibles print as __“remnant”__ and __“survivor”__ is _sarid_ — __“the *remnant* whom the LORD shall call”__ (Joel 2:32) — and it grows from a root meaning *to slip out through the puncture*: the needle's eye Jesus set at the gate was hiding in the word all along (Matthew 19:24).

proposals.rationale: House style forbids author sentences that open with And/But/That.

proposals.old: The Hebrew says the opposite, four times over, in the four words our Bibles render __“remnant”__ — and each one is worth the dig.
proposals.new: The Hebrew says the opposite, four times over, in the four words our Bibles render __“remnant”__ — and each one is worth the work.
proposals.rationale: “Worth the dig” is casual register that slightly undercuts the etymological density of the surrounding paragraph.
